the proposed system is able to select the best camera view to broadcast, in a live environment, based on the location data retrieved from a dynamic 3d model.
we have developed a location-aware system to help technical directors in the task of broadcasting sport events.
we have developed a system that helps technical director to select the best camera to broadcast a sport event.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) the development of a 3D dynamic model of the scenario that is updated with the location information of the moving elements, (2) the development of an interface that allows technical directors to indicate their interest in certain objects, and (3) the design of a mechanism that selects the best views of the scenario based on the information obtained from the 3D dynamic models and the interests of the technical director.
the design, development, and validation of an intelligent system to help technical directors in the selection of the best camera views for a sport event.
the design of an architecture to provide the necessary support for a technical director, and to develop a prototype of the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system provides a technical director with a 3D view of the scenario, with the current position of moving objects and cameras, as well as with a list of cameras ordered by relevance.
the system presented in this paper provides an effective tool for technical directors to help them to make decisions in real time, and to select the best camera views in the broadcasting task.
this system helps in broadcasting sport events in live by providing technical directors with the information they need to make the best decisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present an innovative approach for live broadcasting sport events based on a 3D dynamic model that allows technical directors to select the best camera in run-time.

we have developed a system that allows technical directors to indicate in run-time the kind of views they are interested in (e.g., views of a certain player) and the system is responsible of selecting the cameras whose views should be broadcasted.
we have developed a location-based system to help the technical director to select in run-time the camera views that best fit the interests of a user.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3D model can be used not only for visualizing the scenario, but also for selecting cameras in real time.
, using our system, the technical director can focus on the most interesting aspects of the sport event and let the system manage the rest of the tasks.
the use of a 3D dynamic model can be a powerful tool for the management of a large number of cameras in real-time.
